title: The Afternoon Brief: Panini's fraud claim escalates card-industry fight
dek: Panini unsealed allegations that Fanatics misused confidential licensing data to win NBA and NFL deals. Elsewhere, the Seahawks locked up a Pro-Bowl cornerback, Makhachev chases a UFC record, and cycling mourns a 19-year-old rider.
author: GoCheckMySports
key_fact: The Panini-Fanatics litigation shifted from antitrust theory to specific claims of trade secret theft, setting the stage for discovery battles and a near-term trial-or-settlement decision.
bottom_line: Panini's unsealed fraud allegations transform the card-licensing lawsuit from antitrust theory into claims of trade secret misuse, raising the stakes for discovery and a near-term trial-or-settlement decision. Witherspoon's record extension locks a cornerstone defender to Seattle's championship window. Makhachev pursues history tomorrow night. And cycling's community grieves after a fatal incident during the Volta a Portugal. Watch for Panini's discovery filings on the route any confidential data took, Ohtani's next bullpen session in the two-to-five-day window, Makhachev's title defense outcome, and race organizers' response on safety procedures following Tarling's death.
body: The defining story deepens from this morning: Panini's newly unsealed fraud allegations against Fanatics move the three-year-old antitrust case from broad competitive claims into granular accusations of data misuse. Panini contends Fanatics obtained the precise mechanics of its NBA and NFL licensing deals, royalty rates, minimum guarantee schedules, marketing commitments, autograph spend obligations, and weaponized that information to win exclusive deals worth billions. Fanatics had sought to keep the allegations sealed; a magistrate judge this week unsealed them. The honest read is that Panini's claims are now specific, but the filings do not yet detail the mechanism by which any information changed hands, only what Panini says was obtained and how that knowledge could have influenced Fanatics' bids.

Otherwise, the midday picture spans the roster, the fight game, and losses. The Seattle Seahawks locked Devon Witherspoon, their 25-year-old cornerback and three-time Pro-Bowler, into a four-year, $132 million extension with over $101 million in guaranteed money, making him the highest-paid cornerback in NFL history. Witherspoon starred in the Seahawks' Super Bowl LX championship run, and the deal ties him to the team through his prime immediately after that victory. In combat sports, Islam Makhachev defends his welterweight title tomorrow night in Philadelphia against undefeated Ian Machado Garry, chasing his 17th consecutive victory, one shy of Anderson Silva's UFC record. And in cycling, tragedy struck: NSN's development squad withdrew from the Volta a Portugal on Saturday, one day after the death of 19-year-old Welsh time-trial specialist Finlay Tarling. Local media reports indicated a car entered the race course going in the opposite direction and struck Tarling after the driver missed warning signs from race stewards.

On the field, Australia defeated Japan 56-17 in the second Test in Townsville, securing three consecutive wins for the first time since 2024 under new coach Les Kiss. The Wallabies trailed at halftime before dominating the second half through set piece and breakdown work. In baseball, the Dodgers reported encouraging progress on Shohei Ohtani's left knee: he threw a 35-pitch bullpen session Friday, his first mound work in more than three weeks. Manager Dave Roberts said he is confident another bullpen session will follow within two to five days, after which the recovery path should clarify.
